answer: Each agent must stake a scarce, nontransferable relic credential, then earn influence only through repeated, independently verified work across time; a quartz audit samples claims, while a willow-style recovery path lets honest agents regain access without duplicating stake. Creating many identities does not multiply trust: the attacker must lock fresh capital in every identity and keep each one active long enough to build a record, making large-scale Sybil campaigns costly and slow.
